findings.text: The nested stage two translation helper is the externally visible entry in this lane. It clears prior fault status, succeeds immediately with unchanged result when nested virtualization is inactive for the calling virtual cpu, otherwise initializes walk controls from system registers and delegates to internal page table traversal, preserving non fault status bits from the virtual cpu fault register on failure.

Stage one software walk derives its indexing stride from the configured page shift and derives its top address bound from the regime input size. Each level isolates a distinct slice of the virtual address to form a table offset combined with the current table base, progressing toward larger level numbers until a leaf or fault is reached.

When nested translation is enabled for a stage one walk, table addresses are first translated through the nested stage two machinery with retry propagation on contention. Untranslatable or unreadable intermediate results are reported as stage two attributed faults with the current level encoded. An optional per table filter hook, when present, may observe each table and abort the walk with its own status.

Stage one descriptors distinguish invalid, leaf, and table forms through low order bits and level. Table traversal accumulates hierarchical access and execute restrictions into the result unless hierarchical permission disable is active, extracts the next table base, and rejects out of range outputs as address size faults.

Acceptance of a stage one block leaf depends on granule size and large address support. Four kilobyte granule permits middle levels and permits the initial level only with fifty two bit output support, sixteen kilobyte granule permits a single middle level and an earlier level only with fifty two bit support, and sixty four kilobyte granule permits a middle level and an earlier level only when the large physical address feature is present. Other combinations are treated as translation faults.

Stage one access flag handling optionally sets the flag through an atomic update that respects nested writability and propagates contention for retry, with external aborts during access reported distinctly. A leaf whose flag remains clear after any update is reported as an access fault. Successful leaves expand for contiguity hints, combine output base with address offset to form the physical result, and record non global plus address space identity for applicable regimes.

Nested stage two traversal selects its start level and earliest permissible block level from granule size and the configured start value, with four kilobyte granule using a different mapping than larger granules. Input size outside a mid twenties to forty eight bit window is rejected, and start conditions are further constrained by physical address limits, input versus physical size ordering, and start table entry count bounds.

Nested stage two traversal masks its base address to the architecturally valid range, indexes each level from the intermediate address, and validates descriptor presence, type, and output range at each step. Leaves earlier than the permitted block threshold are rejected, and successful leaves populate output address, mapping size derived from level and stride, readability, writability, level, and descriptor, with contiguity hints widening the effective block.

Nested stage two fault reporting encodes the level in the low bits of the fault status, while output range validation compares against a configured maximum unless the maximum equals forty eight bits, in which case all values pass. Input size is defined as sixty four minus the configured size field.

Guest stage two descriptor loads and conditional stores honor the configured endianness of the guest hypervisor, converting between host and guest byte order in both directions, with stores performed as atomic compare and swap against the previously observed value.

Nested walk controls are sourced from virtualization registers and global limits, including base address, size field, granule derived shift, start level, output limit as the lesser of platform intermediate limit and programmed size mapping, hardware access update enable, and endian mode from the guest hypervisor control register.

Translation granule shift is chosen from the TG zero field with reserved encodings treated as sixty four kilobyte, then validated against advertised stage one and stage two granule support from the machine feature register. Unsupported selections fall back preferring the host page shift, then four, sixteen, and sixty four kilobyte in order, defaulting to host shift if none qualify.

The MMU snapshot structure contains sixty four bit members for lower and upper base registers and primary configuration and attribute indirection and extended configuration and permission indirection and overlay permissions for two privilege levels and system control and nested base plus control, namely ttbr0 and ttbr1 and tcr and mair and tcr2 and pir and pire0 and por_el1 and por_el0 and sctlr and vttbr and vtcr.

Host translation state preservation saves and restores base, configuration, attribute, and control registers, with extended permission and overlay registers handled only when the corresponding platform capabilities are present. Restoration orders a speculation barrier workaround for specific errata before updating guest state.

Privileged address translation fast path temporarily installs the guest protection state for the translation operation and restores the host value afterwards, supporting read and write variants of the privileged stage one operation.

Memory attribute byte pairs inner and outer four bit hints with outer in high nibble. Non cacheable encodes as binary zero one zero zero, write through as one zero zero zero, write back as one one zero zero, write back with allocate hints as one one one one. Values whose outer nibble is zero denote device.

Four bit stage two attributes map to eight bit combined forms with reserved inputs normalized to non cacheable and device inputs shifted to device encodings. Stage one transient write through and write back hints are normalized to non transient before combination, with cacheability resolved to the weaker of the two stages and allocation hints inherited from stage one with special handling for transient origins.
Shareability uses two bit codes with non shareable zero zero, reserved zero one, outer shareable one zero, and inner shareable one one.

Effective shareability forces device and non cacheable memory to outer shareable and maps reserved inputs to non shareable. Stage one shareability comes from the leaf descriptor except for fifty two bit capable walks with smaller granules, where it comes from recorded translation control state. Combined stage shareability prefers outer over inner over non shareable.

Combined stage result encoding reports stage two translation failures as faulted results with fault and second stage indicators plus encoded status. On success it merges stage one and stage two attributes through distinct forced write back and normal paths, honors cache disable by forcing non cacheable for memory, preserves output address bits, and merges shareability from both stages.

Stage one result encoding reports failures with fault status plus page walk and second stage flags, reports disabled translation as identity mapping with device attributes except for a nested cache disable case that reports write back allocate hints with non shareable, and reports enabled translation by indexing the appropriate memory attribute register, forcing non cacheable when caching is disabled, preserving physical bits, and attaching computed shareability.

Privileged access never protection version three is active only when the feature is advertised and either permission indirection is enabled or the regime control enables enhanced privileged access never. Base permissions derive from descriptor user and read only state plus execute never bits with separate rules for host hypervisor regime versus others, augmented by write implies execute never controls and overlay enable flags.

Hierarchical table restrictions further narrow base permissions, with non hypervisor regimes using a two bit table access field to remove combinations of unprivileged and write access and using table execute never bits to narrow privileged and unprivileged execution, while hypervisor regime uses a single table write restrict bit and table execute never to narrow privileged execution.

Software walks operate as level progression machines that may advance to the next level, terminate successfully at a validated leaf, terminate with architecturally classified faults, or request retry on concurrent update contention, with stage one additionally allowing abort through filter or nested fault attribution.

Concurrent descriptor updates require retry handling, atomic compare swap usage, and writability checks before access flag writes. Endianness mismatch, out of range outputs, illegal block levels, uncleared access flags, and speculative translation hazards require explicit barriers, preservation of host protection and translation state, and distinct fault versus abort reporting.
